mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the effect reverses during a recession (UNRATE < 3% simultaneously).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when labor market is strong (UNRATE > 4%).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses wage growth and consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered periods, or the effect inverts when inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 4%) is high.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect disappears during periods of strong demand (GDPC1 YoY growth > 2%).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 5-year averages signals a stagflationary environment, which increases both interest rates and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered stagflation episodes, or the effect reverses when GDP growth (GDPC1 QoQ) is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.2 million units, combined with a concurrent drop in personal savings (RSAFS), signals a housing demand shock that reduces construction and retail activity, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 1.2M AND RSAFS monthly change < -1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when mortgage rates (not directly observed, but implied by FEDFUNDS) are falling.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days in any macro regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained payroll employment growth, or the effect reverses during high inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 5%).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) below their respective 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of monetary easing (FEDFUNDS falling).
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 12-mo MA AND HOUST < 12-mo MA for three consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS not falling (FEDFUNDS change <= 0%)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when FEDFUNDS is falling by more than 0.25% per quarter.
